question: Should OpenClaw add a core agent-governance configuration surface that promises enforceable behavior, or should this be narrowed to explicitly non-security prompt guidance?
rationale: The permanent boundary determines the configuration contract, tool enforcement design, delivery gating, external process execution, and the security claims operators may rely upon; those choices cannot be safely inferred from this implementation.

options.title: Define enforcement architecture first
options.body: Pause this branch and design canonical prompt, tool-policy, pre-delivery validation, schema, and failure semantics before implementing a core governance feature.

options.title: Narrow to prompt guidance
options.body: Remove blocking and validator claims, omit the external exec surface, and expose clearly documented best-effort guidance through the canonical prompt path.

options.title: Sponsor the full policy engine
options.body: Confirm the core feature and require a redesigned branch with complete runtime coverage, security review, compatibility proof, and live demonstrations.

recommendation.title: Define enforcement architecture first
recommendation.body: Pause this branch and design canonical prompt, tool-policy, pre-delivery validation, schema, and failure semantics before implementing a core governance feature.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the canonical agent prompt, configuration architecture, and core runtime boundary, all areas with substantial recent ownership history.
